Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the OmniChip Technologies Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Lee, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Lee, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to OmniChip Technologies’ Q3 earnings call. With me today are Robert Chen, CEO; Susan Davis, CFO; Michael Johnson, COO; and David Rodriguez, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to discuss our capacity expansion plan on the existing fabs for this quarter. Good morning, team. Today's discussion focuses on the crucial capacity expansion initiatives underway at our key fabrication facilities. As you know, demand for our products, particularly in the automotive and IoT sectors, continues to outstrip supply, necessitating these strategic investments. Our capacity expansion plan this quarter centers around three key locations: Fab 12A, our Xiamen facility, and the Tainan complex. The cornerstone of our near-term capacity increase is the ongoing Fab 12A Phase 5 expansion. As previously announced, this phase is specifically designed to augment our 28-nanometer wafer production. We are on track to bring an additional 10,000 wafer starts per month online by the end of this quarter. This incremental capacity is vital for fulfilling backlog orders, particularly in the microcontroller segment, where 28nm technology is a workhorse for a variety of automotive and industrial applications. Financially, this expansion is expected to contribute approximately $80 million in additional revenue per quarter once fully operational. We've allocated a capital expenditure of $250 million for the Fab 12A Phase 5 project, which includes the acquisition and installation of advanced lithography equipment, etching tools, and metrology systems. We anticipate a payback period of approximately 3 years, based on projected average selling prices for 28nm wafers and a 90% utilization rate. It's important to note that the 28nm node, while mature, continues to offer a compelling cost-performance ratio, making it a critical component of our overall product portfolio. Furthermore, we have secured key long-term supply agreements with our equipment vendors to mitigate potential disruptions and ensure a smooth ramp-up of production. Our Xiamen facility is demonstrating strong operational performance and is projected to reach its target capacity of 25,000 WSPM by the end of this quarter. This milestone represents a significant achievement and underscores our commitment to expanding our manufacturing footprint in the Asia-Pacific region. The Xiamen facility primarily focuses on producing components for consumer electronics and communication devices. The Xiamen facility has been crucial for securing market share in China, which saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by robust demand for smartphones and networking equipment. The Xiamen expansion has directly contributed approximately $45 million in revenue this quarter alone. We are actively exploring further expansion opportunities in Xiamen, potentially including the addition of more advanced process nodes to cater to the evolving needs of the Chinese market. We are also closely monitoring geopolitical developments and trade policies to ensure our operations in Xiamen remain resilient and adaptable. Our Tainan facility is undergoing a more substantial two-phased expansion to address long-term demand for advanced semiconductor technologies. Currently, the site has a 90,000 WSPM capacity. Phase 5 is complete, and Phase 6 is under construction. The completion of Phase 5 is projected to bring the total capacity of the 12A site to approximately 90,000 WSPM. This expansion, primarily focused on supporting our leading-edge 7nm and 5nm production, will enable us to meet the growing demand from our high-performance computing and artificial intelligence customers. Looking ahead, Phase 6 is slated to come online in Q4 of next year and will add an additional 30,000 WSPM, bringing the total Tainan facility capacity to approximately 120,000 WSPM. The P6 expansion represents a capital investment of $1.2 billion and includes the installation of extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment, critical for manufacturing advanced chips at the 5nm node. This investment is expected to yield a significant return, with projected annual revenue exceeding $1.5 billion once fully operational. These capacity expansions are not just about adding more production volume; they are strategically aligned with our long-term growth objectives. We are closely monitoring the following KPIs to ensure the success of these initiatives: Wafer Output, Utilization Rate, Cycle Time, Yield Rate, and Return on Invested Capital. While we are optimistic about the potential of these capacity expansions, we also recognize the challenges ahead, including Equipment Lead Times, Skilled Labor Shortage, and Geopolitical Uncertainty. In conclusion, our capacity expansion plan represents a significant investment in our future growth. By strategically expanding our manufacturing footprint and focusing on advanced technologies, we are well-positioned to meet the growing demand for our products and deliver sustainable value to our shareholders. We will continue to monitor the progress of these initiatives closely and provide regular updates on our performance.

We also made meaningful progress with our CapEx guidance for the full year or long term, the changes from the previous guidance, and the comments for this quarter. Good morning, everyone. Let's delve into our Capital Expenditure (CapEx) guidance, focusing primarily on the P6 and P5 expansion projects. As previously communicated, our strategic imperative remains centered on expanding our advanced node capacity and diversifying our geographic footprint to mitigate geopolitical risks and better serve our global customer base. Our previously announced P6 facility in Taiwan remains a critical component of our long-term growth strategy. The total CapEx commitment for P6 is approximately NT$100 billion, allocated across a three-year period spanning 2022-2024. As projected, 2022 represented the peak investment year, accounting for approximately 45% of the total P6 CapEx, or roughly NT$45 billion. This significant outlay was primarily focused on initial land acquisition, foundational infrastructure development, and the procurement of long-lead-time equipment, including advanced lithography systems from ASML. We encountered some minor supply chain delays during Q3 2022, impacting the initial equipment delivery schedule, but these were successfully mitigated through proactive engagement with our vendors and did not materially impact the overall project timeline. We anticipate approximately 30% of the total P6 CapEx, or NT$30 billion, will be deployed in 2023. This year's investment is heavily weighted towards cleanroom construction, utility infrastructure build-out, and the installation of critical process equipment such as etching, deposition, and metrology tools. We are currently tracking slightly ahead of schedule on the cleanroom construction, leading to a potential pull-forward of some equipment installation into Q4 of this year. We are closely monitoring the inflationary pressures on construction materials, but our hedging strategies have proven effective in mitigating significant cost overruns. The remaining 25%, or NT$25 billion, is earmarked for 2024. This final phase focuses on equipment ramp-up, process optimization, and the commencement of initial production runs. We expect P6 to begin contributing meaningfully to revenue in the second half of 2024, initially focusing on the 5nm and 3nm process nodes, catering to high-performance computing and advanced mobile applications. We are also exploring the potential to incorporate advanced packaging capabilities within the P6 facility to provide vertically integrated solutions to our key customers. Turning to the P5 expansion, this project remains crucial for addressing the continued strong demand for mature technology nodes, particularly the 28nm process. Our original budget for the P5 expansion was approximately US$1.5 billion. The primary objective is to add 10,000 wafer starts per month of 28nm capacity. We are pleased to report that due to efficient capital allocation and favorable procurement terms negotiated with our equipment suppliers, we have optimized the P5 expansion budget, reducing the overall CapEx requirement by approximately 5% compared to our initial estimates. This reflects our commitment to maximizing capital efficiency and delivering strong returns on investment. The strategic importance of expanding 28nm capacity at P5 cannot be overstated. This expansion is primarily driven by robust demand from the automotive, industrial, and IoT sectors. These applications require reliable, cost-effective, and power-efficient solutions, making 28nm an ideal technology platform. We are witnessing particularly strong growth in demand from electric vehicle manufacturers for power management ICs and microcontroller units fabricated on the 28nm node. As part of the P5 expansion, we are implementing advanced manufacturing techniques, including predictive maintenance and AI-powered process optimization, to enhance yield, improve cycle times, and reduce overall manufacturing costs. We are also investing in advanced metrology equipment to ensure the highest levels of process control and product quality. Our overall CapEx guidance for the full year remains unchanged at approximately US$6 billion. The slight reduction in the P5 expansion budget is offset by increased investments in advanced packaging technologies across our other facilities. In Q3, we spent approximately US$1.4 billion on CapEx, in line with our expectations. We saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, partially driven by increased capacity utilization at our existing facilities. We are carefully managing our inventory levels and are confident in our ability to meet customer demand in the coming quarters. We believe our CapEx investments are strategically aligned with the long-term growth drivers of the semiconductor industry, including artificial intelligence, 5G, electric vehicles, and the Internet of Things. We are committed to investing in the technologies and infrastructure necessary to maintain our leadership position and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are closely monitoring the macroeconomic environment and geopolitical developments. While we are mindful of the potential risks, we remain confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and execute our strategic plan. We are committed to maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and ensuring that our investments generate strong returns. In summary, our CapEx investments in P6 and P5 are critical for our long-term growth strategy. We are executing these projects on schedule and within budget, and we are confident that they will deliver significant value to our shareholders. We are committed to maintaining a transparent and disciplined approach to capital allocation and providing regular updates on our progress.

On a broader level, our Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons supported our positioning. For the first quarter of 2021, OmniChip Technologies reported revenue of TWD 47.1 billion. This figure represents a solid performance, reflecting both sequential growth and significant year-over-year expansion. We achieved a 4% increase in revenue compared to Q4 2020, moving from TWD 45.3 billion in Q4 to TWD 47.1 billion in Q1. This growth, while moderate, is particularly noteworthy considering the typical seasonal slowdown often experienced in the semiconductor industry during the first quarter. A key driver of this QoQ growth was a greater than 3% increase in the company's average selling price. Specifically, the ASP for our leading-edge 7nm and 5nm processes saw robust growth, contributing approximately 2.5 percentage points to the overall QoQ revenue increase. This increase in ASP was primarily driven by the ongoing global demand for HPC applications, including data centers, AI, and advanced gaming, which fueled a higher demand for our advanced node technologies. Clients were willing to pay a premium to secure capacity. We successfully shifted our product mix towards higher-value, more complex chips. This strategic shift, focusing on advanced nodes and customized solutions, allowed the company to capture higher margins and increase ASP. For example, the proportion of revenue derived from 7nm and below processes increased from 28% in Q4 2020 to 31% in Q1 2021. The global chip shortage further exacerbated the demand-supply imbalance, allowing us to exercise some pricing power. While avoiding excessive price gouging, we strategically optimized pricing based on long-term customer relationships and value-added services. Wafer shipments also contributed positively to the QoQ growth, albeit to a lesser extent than ASP. We experienced a modest increase in wafer shipments, in the range of 1-2%. This increase was primarily attributed to continued operation at near-full capacity utilization across our major fabrication facilities. Several debottlenecking initiatives and minor capacity expansions completed in late 2020 allowed for slightly higher overall wafer output. Despite the overall chip shortage impacting the automotive industry, we experienced continued strong demand for our automotive-grade chips, particularly those used in advanced driver-assistance systems and electric vehicles. The stronger New Taiwan dollar acted as a significant headwind, partially offsetting the positive impact of ASP and wafer shipments. Based on internal estimates, the stronger NT dollar shaved off approximately 1.5 percentage points of potential QoQ revenue growth. Our Q1 2021 revenue of TWD 47.1 billion represents an impressive 11.4% increase compared to TWD 42.3 billion in Q1 2020. This robust YoY growth underscores our strong competitive position and our ability to capitalize on the growing demand for semiconductors. The continued global rollout of 5G infrastructure was a major driver of YoY growth. Our chips are used extensively in 5G base stations, smartphones, and other related devices. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the trend towards digital transformation, boosting demand for semiconductors in various applications, including cloud computing, e-commerce, and remote work solutions. We successfully gained market share in several key segments, particularly in the areas of advanced node technologies and specialty semiconductors. The Internet of Things sector experienced substantial growth, generating increased demand for our chips used in smart home devices, industrial automation, and connected vehicles. Strategic initiatives aimed at increasing market presence in North America and Europe began to yield positive results, contributing to the overall YoY growth. We secured new long-term contracts with major players in these regions. Similar to the QoQ performance, the stronger NT dollar also negatively impacted the YoY revenue growth. Without the FX headwinds, the YoY revenue growth would have been closer to 13-14%. During the Q4 2020 earnings call, we provided revenue guidance for Q1 2021 in the range of TWD 46.5 billion to TWD 47.0 billion. The actual revenue of TWD 47.1 billion slightly exceeded the upper end of the guidance range. The demand for HPC applications proved to be even stronger than initially anticipated, driving higher ASPs and increased wafer shipments. Our continuous efforts to optimize capacity utilization and improve operational efficiency allowed us to squeeze out slightly more output than initially projected. The shift towards higher-value products occurred more rapidly than initially forecasted, resulting in a more favorable product mix and higher overall revenue. The sales and marketing teams effectively executed our growth strategy, securing new orders and strengthening customer relationships. Our Q1 2021 results demonstrate our resilience and our ability to navigate a complex and dynamic market environment. Our strategic focus on advanced node technologies, specialty semiconductors, and geographical expansion is paying off. While the stronger NT dollar remains a headwind, we are actively implementing hedging strategies to mitigate its impact. Furthermore, ongoing investments in capacity expansion and R&D will position the company for continued growth in the years to come. We maintain a positive outlook on our long-term prospects, driven by the secular trends of 5G, AI, IoT, and digital transformation. We anticipate that OmniChip will continue to outperform its peers and deliver strong returns for its shareholders. We do expect Q2 growth to be slightly lower due to planned maintenance across several fabs, but the overall outlook for the year remains very positive.

I’ll now hand it over to Susan to walk you through the financials.

Susan Davis, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons helped drive improvements in our bottom line. Good morning, everyone. Today, I'll be providing a detailed analysis of our gross margin performance for the first quarter of 2021. We saw significant improvement year-over-year and solid progress sequentially. Our Q1 2021 Gross Margin was 26.5%, compared to 19.2% in Q1 2020, a 7.3 percentage point increase. Compared to Q4 2020, where our gross margin was 24.8%, we saw a 1.7 percentage point improvement. Our Gross Profit for Q1 2021 was TWD 12.49 billion, representing 15.2% QoQ Gross Profit Growth. The substantial 7.3 percentage point increase in gross margin compared to Q1 2020 is a result of several converging factors. A significant contributor was the increased adoption and higher revenue contribution from our 28-nanometer technology. In Q1 2020, 28nm accounted for approximately 18% of our total wafer revenue. This increased to 25% in Q1 2021. 28nm yields higher ASPs and better margins due to process maturity and optimized manufacturing. This shift alone contributed an estimated 3.5 percentage points to the overall gross margin improvement. We saw particularly strong demand for 28nm in the automotive and IoT sectors. Over the past year, we've implemented several cost optimization initiatives across our manufacturing facilities. These included investing TWD 500 million in upgrading our energy infrastructure, resulting in a 12% reduction in per-wafer energy consumption at our Fab 3 facility. We renegotiated key contracts with raw material suppliers, securing an average of 8% reduction in material costs, impacting the costs for silicon and specialized gases, which are key inputs into our manufacturing processes. Through rigorous statistical process control and advanced metrology techniques, we achieved a 3% average improvement in wafer yield across our main production lines. The TWD weakened slightly against the USD in Q1 2021 compared to Q1 2020. As a significant portion of our revenue is denominated in USD, this translated to a positive impact on our TWD-reported gross margin, contributing approximately 0.8 percentage points to the YoY increase. Strong demand across several key sectors, including high-performance computing and 5G infrastructure, allowed us to exercise some pricing power, particularly for advanced nodes. We saw an average ASP increase of 5% for our leading-edge technologies. However, we remain mindful of maintaining competitive pricing and long-term customer relationships. While 28nm played a key role, the initial ramp-up of our 16nm FinFET process also contributed positively. Although representing a smaller portion of overall revenue, the higher margins associated with these newer technologies helped to boost the overall gross margin profile. The 1.7 percentage point increase in gross margin from Q4 2020 to Q1 2021 reflects continued momentum in the factors driving the YoY improvement, but also some unique dynamics. Q1 traditionally sees a slight uptick in demand after the holiday season, resulting in higher fab utilization rates. This increased utilization helps to absorb fixed manufacturing costs, thereby improving gross margins. We strategically shifted our product mix towards higher-margin products in Q1, prioritizing allocation to certain customer segments with higher ASPs. The cost reduction initiatives implemented in previous quarters began to yield more substantial benefits in Q1, as processes were optimized and economies of scale were realized. In our Q4 2020 earnings call, we provided gross margin guidance of 25.5% for Q1 2021. Our actual performance of 26.5% exceeded this guidance by 1.0 percentage point. The demand for 28nm technology exceeded our internal forecasts, particularly in the automotive sector, driven by the global chip shortage and increased demand for electric vehicles. We achieved yield improvements on our 16nm FinFET process at a faster rate than initially projected, contributing to higher-than-anticipated gross margins from this technology node. We proactively managed our inventory levels, avoiding potential write-downs and maximizing the value of our existing inventory. Strong demand from North American customers, particularly in the HPC and data center segments, drove significant revenue growth and contributed positively to our overall gross margin. The Asia-Pacific region remained a key growth driver, with particularly strong demand from Chinese customers in the mobile and consumer electronics sectors. The European market showed steady growth, driven by demand for automotive and industrial applications. Our strong gross margin performance in Q1 2021 demonstrates the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives and our ability to adapt to evolving market conditions. We remain committed to investing in advanced technologies, optimizing our manufacturing processes, and expanding our global footprint. Looking ahead, we expect to maintain healthy gross margins throughout the year. While we anticipate some challenges, such as potential fluctuations in currency exchange rates and increased competition, we are confident that our strategic initiatives and operational excellence will enable us to achieve our financial goals. We are providing guidance for Q2 2021 gross margin to be in the range of 26.0% to 27.0%.

Additionally, our wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quanty and ASP for this quarter showed strong improvement. Overall, Q3 2024 demonstrated a solid performance in our wafer sales segment, driven by robust demand in key sectors and strategic initiatives focused on optimizing our product mix and manufacturing efficiencies. Total wafer shipments reached 2.37 million 8-inch equivalent wafers, aligning with our projected targets and representing a 2.5% increase compared to Q2 2024, and a 1.2% increase year-over-year. This growth, although modest, reflects a stabilization in the memory market and continued strong demand in the automotive and industrial sectors. Shipments of 8-inch wafers accounted for approximately 65% of the total volume, totaling 1.54 million wafers. This segment was primarily driven by demand for analog and power management ICs, particularly in the automotive sector. We saw a significant uptick in orders for IGBTs and MOSFETs used in electric vehicle powertrains and charging infrastructure. Specifically, shipments to automotive clients increased by 18% compared to Q2, fueled by increased EV production targets globally. Furthermore, industrial applications contributed significantly, with strong demand for microcontrollers and sensors used in automation systems and IoT devices. We are actively working to expand 8-inch capacity at our Singapore facility by 10% to meet this growing demand, with the expansion expected to be fully operational by Q1 2025. 12-inch wafer shipments represented the remaining 35% of the total volume, amounting to 0.83 million wafers. This segment was primarily focused on advanced logic and memory applications. While the memory market has shown signs of recovery, it remains somewhat volatile. NAND flash memory shipments were up 5% quarter-over-quarter, driven by demand from enterprise SSDs and mobile devices. However, DRAM shipments remained relatively flat, reflecting ongoing inventory corrections within the PC and mobile segments. On the logic side, we saw strong demand for wafers used in AI accelerators and high-performance computing applications. This area is a key growth driver for our 12-inch wafer business, and we are actively investing in advanced packaging technologies to further enhance our capabilities in this space. A specific example is our collaboration with a leading AI chip designer to develop a novel 2.5D packaging solution using our state-of-the-art fan-out wafer-level packaging technology. The average selling price for wafers across all diameters increased by approximately 3.2% this quarter. This improvement was driven by a combination of factors. We strategically shifted our production mix towards higher-value wafers, particularly those used in automotive, industrial, and AI applications. These wafers typically command higher ASPs due to their stringent quality requirements and advanced process technologies. We maintained a disciplined approach to pricing, focusing on value-based selling and highlighting the benefits of our advanced technologies and superior quality. Ongoing cost reduction initiatives across our manufacturing operations helped improve our gross margins, allowing us to maintain competitive pricing while still capturing a higher ASP. These initiatives included optimizing our energy consumption, improving process yields, and streamlining our supply chain. Specifically, our "Green Fab" initiative, aimed at reducing our carbon footprint, has also yielded significant cost savings in terms of energy and water consumption. Favorable currency fluctuations, particularly the weakening of the Euro against the US dollar, contributed positively to our ASP in Euro-denominated sales. We have hedged a significant portion of our foreign currency exposure to mitigate the impact of future fluctuations. Successful implementation of next generation technology nodes for our clients allowed for increased revenue generation. For example, introduction of FinFET 7nm wafers for a leading AI client led to a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion for that segment. The Asia-Pacific region remained our largest market, accounting for approximately 60% of total wafer sales. China continues to be a key growth driver, although geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions pose ongoing challenges. We are closely monitoring the situation and adapting our strategies accordingly. North America showed strong growth, driven by demand from the automotive and industrial sectors. The US government's incentives for domestic semiconductor manufacturing are creating new opportunities for us to expand our presence in this region. Europe experienced moderate growth, with demand primarily driven by automotive and industrial applications. The European Union's focus on strategic autonomy in semiconductors is creating new opportunities for local suppliers. Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the long-term growth prospects for the wafer market. We are focused on the following key initiatives to drive future growth: Expanding Capacity, Developing Advanced Technologies, Strengthening Customer Relationships, and ESG Initiatives. In conclusion, our Q3 2024 wafer sales performance reflects a solid execution of our strategic priorities and a favorable market environment. While challenges remain, we are confident in our ability to continue to drive growth and create value for our shareholders.

Let's also discuss our overall wafer ASP comments, and the by node or segment wafer ASP comments for this quarter, where we’ve increased efficiency. Good morning, everyone. Let's dive into the wafer Average Selling Price (ASP) performance for Q3 2024. As previously mentioned, we saw a robust increase of over 3% quarter-over-quarter in overall wafer ASP. This is a significant achievement and reflects the strong demand environment coupled with our strategic focus on value extraction. Looking ahead, we are increasing our full-year ASP growth forecast to the high single digits year-over-year, approaching 10%. This upward revision is based on sustained momentum in key market segments and the successful implementation of our pricing strategies. Let\u2019s break down the ASP performance by technology node and key application segments. This continues to be a significant driver of our overall ASP growth. We witnessed a 4.5% QoQ increase in ASP for 7nm and 6nm wafers. This was primarily fueled by increased demand from the high-performance computing sector, particularly for AI accelerators and advanced server CPUs. A key factor was the successful ramp-up of our next-generation EUV-based 6nm process, which commands a premium due to its superior performance and power efficiency. We saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. ASPs for 5nm and 4nm nodes saw an even stronger surge, growing by 6% QoQ. This was driven by strong adoption in the premium smartphone market and the initial ramp of our advanced automotive applications. Our 4nm node, leveraging advanced FinFET technology, is proving particularly attractive for its power efficiency in mobile applications. We are currently working closely with our key customers to optimize their designs for our 4nm process, which is expected to further boost ASPs in the coming quarters. While still in the early stages of production, our 3nm node is already contributing positively to our blended ASP. While volumes are low, the ASP for 3nm wafers is significantly higher than previous generations, reflecting the complexity and cost of manufacturing these advanced chips. We are seeing strong interest in our 3nm node from customers in the HPC and mobile segments, and we expect to see a more significant contribution to our overall ASP in 2025 as production ramps up. While not driving the same level of growth as leading-edge nodes, mature nodes still play a crucial role in our overall revenue and profitability. We saw a slight ASP increase of around 1% QoQ for 28nm wafers. This was primarily driven by increased demand from the IoT and automotive sectors. The ongoing global chip shortage continues to support pricing in this segment. We are also focused on improving our manufacturing efficiency to maintain profitability in this segment. ASPs for 40nm-65nm remained relatively stable, with only minor fluctuations. We are actively managing our capacity in these nodes to align with customer demand. We are also exploring opportunities to optimize our manufacturing processes to reduce costs and improve profitability. The automotive sector continues to be a key growth driver for our mature and specialty nodes. We are seeing strong demand for our power management ICs, microcontrollers, and sensors used in electric vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems. We saw a significant ASP increase in this segment, driven by the increasing complexity of automotive chips and the growing demand for higher-performance solutions. The IoT segment is also contributing to our ASP growth, particularly for our low-power microcontrollers and connectivity solutions. We are seeing strong demand from a wide range of applications, including smart home devices, industrial sensors, and wearable electronics. The industrial segment continues to be a stable source of revenue and profitability. We are seeing strong demand for our power management ICs, motor controllers, and sensors used in industrial automation and equipment. From a regional perspective, we saw particularly strong ASP growth in North America and Asia-Pacific. The strong demand from North American HPC and automotive customers was a key driver of our overall ASP growth. In Asia-Pacific, we saw increased demand from the smartphone and consumer electronics sectors. Our successful ASP performance is a result of several strategic initiatives: Technology Leadership, Value-Based Pricing, Customer Collaboration, and Capacity Management. In conclusion, our Q3 2024 wafer ASP performance was strong, driven by robust demand for our advanced technology nodes and our strategic focus on value extraction. We are confident that we can maintain this momentum in the coming quarters and achieve our full-year ASP growth target. We will continue to invest in advanced technology nodes, implement value-based pricing strategies, and collaborate closely with our customers to deliver exceptional value. We remain optimistic about the long-term growth prospects for the semiconductor industry and our ability to capitalize on these opportunities.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael to provide color on execution.

Michael Johnson, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our capacity expansion plan on the existing fabs for this quarter, which allowed us to meet increased demand.

We also saw execution gains related to our wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quanty and ASP for this quarter, including improved logistics and reduced cycle times.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to our sales by segment or platforms, their respective margin levels, and their respective management comments, where early signs are promising. Now I’ll turn it over to David to discuss technology.

David Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with our CapEx guidance for the full year or long term, especially regarding EUV lithography integration.
 
We also rolled out enhancements supporting our overall wafer ASP comments, enabling us to optimize pricing based on performance tiers.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable our Net margin and Diluted EPS results, allowing for more accurate cost allocation and profitability analysis.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Robert Chen:
We've built strong relationships with key customers in growing markets and are strategically investing in the technologies that will drive future demand, so we expect to maintain this positive trajectory.

Analyst 2:
On Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, is this sustainable in the long term, and what initiatives are in place to maintain or improve it?

Susan Davis:
We are continuously working on cost optimization and are focused on increasing revenue from advanced nodes, which will help us maintain our gross margin.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with sales by segment or platforms, their respective margin levels, and their respective management comments?

Michael Johnson:
We are seeing strong interest in our new AI platform, and we are working closely with key customers to refine our offerings.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in Net margin and Diluted EPS results?

David Rodriguez:
We are making investments in R&D and in improving our operational efficiencies to ensure that we can continue to grow our net margin and EPS. To dive into a more in-depth analysis of the company's net margin and diluted EPS performance, we'll expand upon the reported TWD 10.43 billion net income attributable to the stockholder of the parent and the TWD 0.85 earnings per ordinary share. Our analysis indicates that TechForward Solutions' net margin for the quarter stood at 12.7%, a significant improvement compared to 8.9% in the same quarter last year and 11.2% in the previous quarter. This expansion is primarily attributable to a confluence of factors. Strategic initiatives in the past year streamlined operations. A key driver was the successful rollout of their "Project Phoenix" initiative, a multi-million dollar investment in automating supply chain management and optimizing manufacturing processes. We estimate that "Project Phoenix" contributed approximately 1.5 percentage points to the net margin improvement this quarter alone. Specifically, the company reduced material waste by 7% and improved inventory turnover by 12%, leading to significant cost savings. The company experienced a shift in product mix towards higher-margin products. The launch of their new line of enterprise AI solutions, the "CogniServe" suite, has been particularly successful. These solutions carry significantly higher margins compared to their traditional hardware offerings. CogniServe contributed approximately 22% to the company's overall revenue this quarter, up from 15% in the previous quarter. We actually benefited slightly from favorable currency fluctuations. The strengthening of the TWD against certain regional currencies, particularly the Indonesian Rupiah and the Philippine Peso positively impacted their net income by an estimated 0.3 percentage points. Refinancing their debt at lower interest rates in the previous quarter resulted in a reduction in interest expense, contributing marginally to the net margin improvement, adding approximately 0.2 percentage points. The reported EPS of TWD 0.85 per ordinary share is indeed impressive, especially when considering the dramatic growth from TWD 0.19 in Q1 2020. The jump from TWD 0.19 in Q1 2020 to TWD 0.85 this quarter represents a staggering 347% increase. While this growth rate is unlikely to be sustainable in the long term, it clearly demonstrates the effectiveness of TechForward Solutions' strategic pivot towards higher-growth, higher-margin business segments. The prior EPS figure of TWD 0.19 in Q1 2020 was significantly impacted by the initial stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, which disrupted supply chains and led to a slowdown in demand for their traditional hardware products. Fluctuations in the TWD/USD exchange rate will directly impact the reported ADS EPS. It's important to note that the diluted EPS figure accounts for the potential dilution from outstanding stock options and convertible securities. Management has indicated that there were approximately 12.2 billion weighted average diluted shares outstanding during the quarter. Any significant changes in the number of diluted shares outstanding in future quarters could impact EPS growth. The Southeast Asian market contributed significantly to the EPS growth. Q2 2021 saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion due to increased demand for their AI solutions, particularly in the financial services and healthcare sectors. In contrast, their North American market experienced slower growth of around 7%, primarily due to increased competition and longer sales cycles. TechForward Solutions is actively investing in R&D, particularly in the areas of edge computing and quantum computing. These investments, while potentially impacting near-term profitability, are crucial for maintaining a competitive edge in the long term. Management has guided for continued EPS growth in the next quarter, albeit at a more moderate pace, projecting an EPS range of TWD 0.88 to TWD 0.92. This guidance assumes continued strength in the Southeast Asian market and a gradual recovery in North America.

aspect_summary.CapEx guidance for the full year or long: The CapEx for P6 is NT$100 billion across 2022-2024. 2022 saw 45% investment, 2023 will see 30%, and 2024 will see the remaining 25%. The P5 expansion budget was optimized, reducing the overall CapEx requirement by approximately 5% compared to initial estimates. Overall CapEx guidance for the full year remains unchanged at approximately US$6 billion. Q3 CapEx spend was approximately US$1.4 billion.
aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Q1 2021 revenue was TWD 47.1 billion, a 4% QoQ increase and an 11.4% YoY increase. QoQ growth was driven by a greater than 3% increase in ASP for 7nm and 5nm processes. YoY growth was driven by 5G infrastructure rollout and digital transformation. Revenue slightly exceeded the upper end of the guidance range (TWD 46.5 billion to TWD 47.0 billion). Q2 growth is expected to be slightly lower due to planned maintenance.
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Q1 2021 gross margin was 26.5%, compared to 19.2% in Q1 2020 (7.3 percentage point increase) and 24.8% in Q4 2020 (1.7 percentage point increase). The average selling price for wafers increased by approximately 3.2% this quarter.
aspect_summary.overall wafer ASP comments, and the by n: Overall wafer ASP increased by over 3% QoQ. Full-year ASP growth forecast increased to the high single digits year-over-year. ASP for 3nm wafers is significantly higher than previous generations. 28nm wafer ASPs saw a slight increase of around 1% QoQ.
